q-pr-collocation.label: Preposition in a fixed phrase
q-pr-collocation.summary: Many nouns and verbs take a particular preposition: under pressure, under conditions, in danger, on duty.

q-pr-gerund.label: Noun + preposition + -ing
q-pr-gerund.summary: After a noun such as reputation, habit, chance, way, the preposition is followed by -ing, not by to + verb.

q-pr-object.label: Verbs that take the person directly
q-pr-object.summary: Ask, tell, request, advise take the person with no preposition: asked the student to submit.

rules.text: Learn the preposition with the noun: under conditions / pressure / circumstances, in danger, on duty, at risk. The wrong options are real prepositions that do not belong with the word.
rules.ok: It may occur under prolonged drought conditions.
rules.bad: It may occur towards prolonged drought conditions.

rules.text: After reputation, habit, chance, possibility, way, experience + of, the verb takes -ing: reputation of being honest. 'Reputation to be' is wrong.
rules.ok: She has the reputation of being an honest leader.
rules.bad: She has the reputation to be an honest leader.

rules.text: Verbs such as ask, tell, request, advise, order take the person directly as their object and add 'to' only for the action: asked the student to submit. Do not put 'to' between the verb and the person.
rules.ok: The teacher asked the student to submit the papers.
rules.bad: The teacher asked to the student to submit the papers.

q-pr-collocation.cue: A blank before a noun phrase (conditions, pressure, circumstances) in a short sentence.
q-pr-collocation.standard: Say the phrase with each option; the one that sounds like a stored phrase is the answer.
q-pr-collocation.fast: Think of the noun's usual company: conditions go with under; pressure goes with under.
q-pr-collocation.eliminate: Cross out prepositions of direction (towards) and of time that do not fit the noun.
traps: Two options may be possible in loose English (amidst); the stored phrase wins.
Between needs two things; it is wrong with a single noun phrase.

q-pr-gerund.cue: A noun like reputation / chance / habit followed by 'to' + verb that you must replace.
q-pr-gerund.standard: Replace 'to be' with 'of being' after the noun. Check the article of the next noun.
q-pr-gerund.fast: Pick the option starting with 'of being' / 'of having' after a noun.
q-pr-gerund.eliminate: Remove options that turn the verb into a noun (to have honesty) or keep to + verb.
traps: 'The honest leader' (with the) changes the meaning to one specific leader.
'To be honesty' mixes a verb and a noun.

q-pr-object.cue: 'asked to the student', 'told to him', 'requested to them' in the given sentence.
q-pr-object.standard: Delete the extra 'to' before the person. Keep 'to' only before the action verb.
q-pr-object.fast: Choose the option with no 'to' between the verb and the person.
q-pr-object.eliminate: Drop options with 'that' + base verb for ask, or with 'told to'.
traps: Using 'to' before the person (asked to the student).
Dropping the article in the object (submit papers vs the papers).

pyqs.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
Even though the phenomenon is uncommon, it may still occur ___ prolonged drought conditions.
pyqs.why: 'Occur under [certain] conditions' is the standard phrase: events happen under conditions.

a.note: 'Towards' shows direction and does not go with 'conditions'.

b.note: 'Amidst' is understandable, but 'occur under ... conditions' is the stored phrase the test expects.

c.note: 'Between' needs two things; there is one noun phrase here.

pyqs.caution: 'Amidst prolonged drought conditions' is also acceptable in loose English. The key 'under' rests on the stored phrase 'under conditions'.

pyqs.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
She has the reputation [[to be an honest leader]].
pyqs.why: After the noun 'reputation' the preposition 'of' is used, followed by -ing: 'of being an honest leader'.

a.note: 'To have honesty' keeps the wrong 'to' and changes the meaning.

c.note: 'Of being' is right, but 'the honest leader' points to one particular leader; the sentence speaks of being an honest leader in general.

d.note: 'To be honesty' mixes a verb and a noun and keeps the wrong 'to'.

pyqs.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
The teacher [[asked to the student to submit the papers]].
options: asked the student that submit the papers
requested the student to submit papers
asked the student to submit the papers
told to the student submit papers
pyqs.why: 'Ask' takes the person directly, with no 'to' before the student, and 'to' only before the action: 'asked the student to submit the papers'.

a.note: 'Ask ... that submit' is not a correct pattern.

b.note: 'Requested the student to submit papers' is grammatical, but it drops 'the' from 'the papers' and changes the verb, so it is not the closest correction.

d.note: 'Told to the student' repeats the extra 'to' and has no 'to' before 'submit'.

pyqs.caution: Option b is grammatical too. The key is the option that makes the smallest change (just delete the extra 'to').

practice.text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank.
The workers continued to build the bridge ___ difficult circumstances.

d.note: 'Beside' means next to a thing, not 'in the situation of'.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
He has the habit [[to wake up at five]].
practice.why: After the noun 'habit' use 'of' + -ing: 'of waking up at five'.

c.note: 'For wake' uses a bare verb after a preposition.

d.note: The preposition 'of' is right but the verb must be -ing, not bare.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
There is no chance [[to win the match]] now.
practice.why: After 'no chance' you can use 'of' + -ing: 'of winning the match'. ('A chance to win' is also correct, but it is not among the options.)

b.note: 'For won' uses a past form after a preposition.

d.note: 'That win' misses a subject and the verb is in the wrong form.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
The manager [[told to the clerk to send the file]].
options: told the clerk to send the file
said the clerk to send the file
told the clerk send the file
told to send the file the clerk
practice.why: 'Told' takes the person directly, then 'to' before the action.

b.note: 'Said' cannot take 'the clerk' directly as its object.

c.note: The extra 'to' is removed, but the 'to' before 'send' is lost too.

d.note: The action 'send the file' is placed before the person 'the clerk', an order English does not allow after 'told'.
